_README: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Volare / P50B 26S21P project.
MATLAB, Python and the Mission Control browser engine all read this file.
Change a number here and it changes everywhere. Do not hard-code physical
Every physical parameter is an object:
s  provenance tag, see provenance_tags below
n  optional note explaining the choice
Keys starting with _ are documentation and are ignored by the readers.
MEASURED CURVE DATA lives in params/cells/p50b.json (OCV, R0(SOC,T),
entropic dU/dT, discharge curves, cycle life) because it is bulky and

provenance_tags.MEASURED: Measured in-house on this project's hardware. Highest confidence.
provenance_tags.DATASHEET: Direct from a manufacturer datasheet held in 04_data/.
provenance_tags.DIGITISED: Traced from a manufacturer datasheet plot. Real data, with tracing error.
provenance_tags.CALCULATED: Derived from other parameters in this file.
provenance_tags.DESIGN_CHOICE: A value the team selected. Not a physical constant; free to change.
provenance_tags.PLACEHOLDER: Invented to let the model run. NOT quotable. Must be replaced.

meta.rules_document: Monaco Energy Class Technical Rules 2026.1, issued 08/09/2025

cell._note: Scalar cell properties. Curves are in params/cells/p50b.json.

capacity_min_Ah.n: Guaranteed minimum. Use for worst-case range.

mass_kg.n: Published values span 68-71 g. Weigh a sample lot: 3 g is 1.6 kg across the pack.

i_max_discharge_A.n: 12 C continuous, quoted to a 70 degC cut-off.

ac_impedance_1kHz_ohm.n: Production screening figure. DO NOT use for loss or thermal work - it is roughly half the DC value and using it halves predicted heat.

dcir_ref_ohm.n: Datasheet DCIR. Cross-check: the digitised R0 map in cells/p50b.json gives 11.64 mOhm at 50% SOC / 23 degC, which agrees to 9%.

k_radial_W_mK.n: Across the jelly roll. Dominates side-cooled designs.

k_axial_W_mK.n: Along the windings. Dominates END-cooled designs - which is what this pack uses.

R_core_can_KW.n: Radial core-to-can. Your thermistor reads the can; your safety limit applies to the core. Tune against an instrumented module.

core_mass_fraction.n: Thermal mass split, core vs can.

R1_ref_ohm.n: Charge-transfer RC branch. LOW confidence - needs HPPC.

R2_ref_ohm.n: Diffusion RC branch. LOW confidence - needs HPPC.

Ea_over_R_K.n: Arrhenius activation for R0, FITTED from the digitised temperature-series curves over 0-60 degC by tools/export_cell_tables.py. Supersedes the 2500 K that was previously assumed - the assumption was 2x the measured value, and this parameter governs the whole thermal-feedback question. Restricted to 0-60 degC on purpose: one exponent cannot span -40 to +60, because the low-temperature rise is a different mechanism.

T_discharge_min_C.n: Typical high-power NMC. Confirm on the controlled datasheet.

T_charge_min_C.n: Charging below 0 degC risks lithium plating.

T_cutoff_C.n: The 60 A rating is quoted to this cut-off.

T_warn_C.n: Working ceiling. Cycle life over the season, not a safety limit.

pack._note: 26S21P in TWO LAYERS of 13 groups. Each group is 3 rows x 7 columns.

grid_rows.n: Group slot grid, ROWS. Changed from 4x4 to 5x3 because the 4x4 container is 765 mm long and the pod has only 670 mm that is both tall enough and aft of the ENERGY_REQ_50 bulkhead. cad/scripts/pack_fit.py sweeps every grid that can hold 13 slots per layer; 5x3 is the only one that fits, and it also shortens the series path by 5%.

grid_cols.n: Group slot grid, COLUMNS. See grid_rows. 15 slots per layer for 13 groups, leaving 2 per layer for the BMS, contactor and fuse.

cell_clearance_m.n: Cell-to-cell edge gap. Too narrow for a coolant tube - this is why the pack is end-cooled, not side-cooled. See cooling._architecture.

group_clearance_x_m.n: Carries the series interconnect at pack potential.

non_cell_mass_fraction.n: Holders, busbars, enclosure, cold plates, BMS, harness as a fraction of cell mass. Replace with a measured build.

h_internal_W_m2K.n: Natural convection inside a sealed enclosure.

busbar._note: Interconnect: cell-to-busbar joints, collector rails, manifolds, series links.

rail_width_m.n: The segment beside the centre feed carries 3 cells' worth: 55 A at the worst legal case, needing 11 mm2. 6 mm x 1.5 mm gave only 9 mm2.

manifold_width_m.n: Carries up to two thirds of group current.

series_link_width_m.n: Sized so the 450 A continuous rating exceeds the 385 A worst legal draw AND sits above the 400 A fuse, as Monaco ENERGY_REQ_59 requires.

routing_factor.n: Straight-line length understates a real bar with bend radii.

weld_resistance_ohm.n: 1092 joints in the pack, 16% of interconnect resistance. Four-wire measurement on one scrap joint would settle it - cheapest high-value test in the project.

operating_temp_C.n: Busbars in a sealed pack run hotter than expected. 15.7% more resistance than the 20 degC handbook value.

cu_rho_20C_ohm_m.n: Annealed copper, IEC 60228. A MATERIAL property, shared by the busbars and the HV harness -- the busbar. prefix is historical, not a statement about where it applies.

density_limit_cont_A_mm2.n: Sustained, still air, limited convection. Rule of thumb, not a standard.

density_limit_peak_A_mm2.n: Momentary only; needs a demonstrated short duty cycle.

_architecture: END (AXIAL) COOLING VIA COLD PLATES - not side cooling.
WHY. In the flat 26x21 layout the coolant tubes sat in the inter-row
gaps. That cannot be done here. In the two-layer pack the gap between
cell rows INSIDE a group is 2.0 mm, and a 6 mm tube does not fit. Only
the 12 mm inter-group gaps could take a tube, and those reach just the
outer row of each 3-row group - leaving the centre row of all 26 groups
with no adjacent tube. That is the orphaned-row failure mode from the
flat study, but affecting a third of the pack instead of one row.
The geometry instead offers something better. Cylindrical cells conduct
roughly 30x better along the winding axis (25 W/m.K) than across it
(0.85 W/m.K), and the two-layer stack already has three natural plate
planes: below layer 1, between the layers, and above layer 2. Cooling
the cell ENDS uses the good conduction path and reaches every cell
equally - no orphans possible.
Layer 1 is cooled at both ends by the base plate and the interlayer
plate. Layer 2 likewise by the interlayer and lid plates. The interlayer
plate serves both, so it carries twice the duty.
EVERYTHING ELSE FROM THE FLAT MODEL IS RETAINED: serpentine tubes
grouped into parallel hydraulic circuits, Reynolds/Nusselt regime
detection, Dittus-Boelter turbulent h, Darcy-Weisbach pressure drop with
bend losses, coolant advection so the fluid warms along the path, and
counter-flow routing on alternate circuits.

tubes_per_plate.n: Serpentine passes across the plate. Sets wetted length and hence velocity for a given flow.

n_circuits.n: The flat-layout study found a sharp optimum at 3: Re just below the turbulent transition, good h, and 0.24 bar. 2 circuits buys 0.2 K for 3x the pressure; 5 falls off the laminar cliff. Re-verify for this plate geometry.

interleave_circuits.n: Spread each circuit across the pack rather than giving it one region.

counter_flow.n: Reverse alternate circuits. Peak temperature is unchanged - that is set by total heat removal - but spread drops ~16%, and spread drives SOC divergence and differential ageing.

K_bend.n: Minor loss coefficient per 180 degree bend.

fluid.n: The flat study found 50/50 glycol is ~3x the viscosity of water and drags the flow toward laminar, costing 0.7 K at sustained power. Freeze protection is not a requirement in Monaco in July; corrosion inhibition is, and is bought separately.

mu_Pa_s.n: Water at 30 degC. 50/50 glycol would be 0.0025.

k_W_mK.n: Water at 30 degC. 50/50 glycol would be 0.38.

R_can_plate_KW.n: Cell end face to plate through the thermal interface pad. Cannot be calculated to useful accuracy - bond-line thickness and fill fraction dominate. Measure on an instrumented module.

R_plate_tubewall_KW.n: Through the plate to the embedded tube wall.

cell_ends_cooled.n: Both ends of every cell contact a plate in this stack-up.

gap_filler_k_W_mK.n: Potting compound between cell cans. Air only would be 0.03.

gap_contact_frac.n: Effective conduction area fraction between adjacent cans.

_R_cell_coolant_note: Cell-to-coolant thermal resistance, per cell, for the END-PLATE pack.
This is here because MATLAB and Python disagreed by a factor of five
and nothing noticed. P50B_ThermalDesign carried a hard-coded 5.0 K/W
with a comment describing a BOTTOM-COOLED cell 'through holder and
TIM' -- an accurate description of the flat, side-cooled layout this
project abandoned, left behind when the architecture changed to
end plates. Python's resolved model gives 0.909 K/W for the pack that
actually exists, and the README has been quoting that figure all
along.
The consequence was not cosmetic: the mission integrator drove cell
temperature through the stale number, so every MATLAB temperature
rise was about 5.5x too pessimistic, including the one behind the
ENERGY_REQ_93 exposed-parts check.
The split below is:
solid  (R_can_plate + R_plate_tubewall) / cells_ends_cooled
-- pure arithmetic on the parameters above, so MATLAB can
and does recompute it rather than trusting this value.
conv   the convective film, which needs the resolved tube
hydraulics in python/volare/layout3d.py. It is derived
once, like the cell curves in params/cells/, and it MOVES
WITH FLOW RATE -- rerun the derivation if
cooling.flow_L_per_min changes.
tools/crosscheck.py compares the total, so the two implementations
cannot drift apart again silently.

R_solid_cell_KW.n: (R_can_plate + R_plate_tubewall) / cell_ends_cooled. Both ends of every cell reach a plate.

R_conv_cell_KW.n: Convective film, per cell, from the resolved tube hydraulics at cooling.flow_L_per_min. Derived by python/volare/layout3d.py hydraulics(). Rerun if the flow rate changes.

R_cell_coolant_KW.n: Total per-cell resistance to coolant for the end-plate pack. Replaces the 5.0 K/W bottom-cooled figure P50B_ThermalDesign used to hard-code.

motor._note: Competr counter-rotating electric outboard. Axial-flux PMSM, water cooled.

power_nominal_W.n: 26.9 kW (40 HP). EXCEEDS the Monaco 25 kW limit - see configured_power_limit_W.

power_max_W.n: Hardware peak. NOT a permitted operating point: ENERGY_REQ_188 v1.1 caps instantaneous power at motor.power_limit_W and forbids peaks. The controller limit is what makes this outboard legal.

mass_kg.n: Outboard only. Trim assembly adds 10 kg.

bus_v_nominal_V.n: Competr stock pack. The P50B 26S gives 93.6 V.

bus_v_max_V.n: At 100% SoC. Equals 26 x 4.2 V exactly - confirms 26S.

configured_power_limit_W.n: MONACO ENERGY_REQ_188 HARD CAP. Applied to motor ELECTRICAL input, not shaft power - a shaft cap of 25 kW would draw 26.9 kW and break the rule. Enforced by bisection in the drivetrain solver.

pole_pairs.n: Axial-flux marine machines commonly 8-14. Sets electrical frequency.

peak_efficiency.n: Phase resistance is BACK-SOLVED from this so the loss model reproduces it. Assuming a resistance and separately declaring an efficiency is how a model ends up reporting 89% while claiming 95.5%.

winding_temp_calib_C.n: Temperature at which the loss model is evaluated.

_speed_note: THE COMPETR DATASHEET STATES NO MOTOR SPEED ANYWHERE.
It gives 26.9 kW nominal, 42 kW maximum and 100 N.m maximum torque,
and stops. Every speed in this model is therefore inferred, and two
different inferences are in circulation:
4000 rpm   this file, back-solved from the datasheet's own numbers.
P = 2*pi*n*Q puts 42 kW at 100 N.m at 4011 rpm, so the
datasheet's peak power is only reachable at or above
that speed.
2500 rpm   the figure in the hydrodynamics team's brief, with
1300 rpm nominal. Their tool flags that at 2500 rpm and
100 N.m the ceiling is 26.18 kW, so the datasheet's
42 kW is unreachable, and that 25 kW cannot be made at
the quoted 1300 rpm nominal either -- the ceiling there
is 13.61 kW.
These cannot both be right, and the datasheet cannot be right on its
own terms unless the maximum speed is at least 4011 rpm. Two
independent teams reached the same conclusion from different ends,
which is worth something.
Nothing here has been quietly reconciled. The value used is 4000 rpm
because it is the only one consistent with the datasheet this project
holds; the brief's figure is carried beside it so the conflict stays
visible, and P50B_MotorSpecAudit prints both every time it runs.
ONE EMAIL TO COMPETR SETTLES THIS. Ask for the torque-speed envelope
and the maximum continuous speed. It is the cheapest open question in
the project and it gates the gearbox ratio, which gates the propeller,
which gates the boat speed.

max_speed_rpm.n: Back-solved from the datasheet: 42 kW at 100 N*m needs 4011 rpm. See _speed_note - the datasheet states no speed, and the hydrodynamics brief says 2500.

max_speed_rpm_brief.n: The conflicting figure from the hydrodynamics team's brief. Carried so the disagreement is visible, not used by the model.

nominal_speed_rpm_brief.n: Also from their brief. At 1300 rpm and 100 N*m the power ceiling is 13.6 kW, so the 25 kW nominal cannot be produced there. Their audit says so explicitly.

gearbox_ratio.n: Datasheet confirms a gearbox exists but not its ratio.

R_case_sea_KW.n: Submerged outboard - the sea is an excellent heat sink and the reason it takes this power at all.

R_wind_coolant_KW.n: Winding to COOLANT, the whole path, used by the drivetrain thermal check. Distinct from R_wind_case_KW, which is only winding to case -- adding the two would double-count the case.

coolant_inlet_max_C.n: Highest coolant inlet temperature the motor is assumed to tolerate. Confirm with Competr; it bounds how hard the pack and the motor can share one loop.

power_limit_W.n: Enforced controller limit. The choice is ours; the reason is ENERGY_REQ_188 v1.1, which caps the sum of INSTANTANEOUS power of all motors at 25 kW and permits no peak. The Competr outboard is rated above this, so the controller must hard-limit and the limit must be demonstrable to the Technical Committee. Distinct from motor.power_max_W, which is the hardware peak and is not a permitted operating point.

inverter._note: NOT SELECTED. Competr lists it as 'on request'. These parameters describe a representative device; the sizing requirements above them follow from the motor and pack and do not depend on the choice.

status.v: OPEN - Competr datasheet lists inverter as 'on request'

technology.n: At a 93.6 V bus the drive is conduction-dominated, not switching-dominated, so on-resistance matters far more than switching energy.

Vce0_V.n: Zero for a MOSFET channel; ~0.8 V for an IGBT.

Rds_on_tempco.n: Multiplier at 125 degC junction. Using the cold value understates loss by ~60%.

E_ref_voltage_V.n: At 93.6 V the switching term scales down ~4.3x from this.

dc_link_ripple_coeff.n: Peak DC-link RMS ripple as a fraction of phase RMS.

R_hs_coolant_KW.n: The inverter rejects into the same coolant loop as the pack and competes with it.

harness._note: Pack terminals to inverter DC terminals. Series resistance in the same circuit as the busbars.

cable_area_mm2.n: 70 mm2 derates to only 214 A and could not carry the current. 150 mm2 gives 459 A derated against a 385 A worst legal draw.

cable_conductor.n: Tinned for marine corrosion; flexible for hull vibration.

base_ampacity_A_mm2.n: Free air, 105 degC insulation, 30 degC ambient. Cross-check against ABYC E-11 or ISO 13297.

fuse_rating_A.n: Monaco ENERGY_REQ_59 requires protection at or below the continuous rating of everything it protects: busbar 450 A, cable 459 A. Also clears the 385 A worst legal draw. Needs a coordination study against the short-circuit capability of a 21P group.

fuse_resistance_ohm.n: Cold. Rises substantially as the element heats.

contactor_resistance_ohm.n: Degrades over life; check on a maintenance schedule.

n_bolted_joints.n: Pack terminal x2, fuse x2, contactor x2.

R_per_bolted_joint_ohm.n: Clean, correctly torqued, anti-oxidant treated. A loose or corroded joint can be 10-50x this and is a fire risk, not just a loss.

auxiliary._note: 12 V loads, supplied from the traction pack through the Competr DC/DC.

dcdc_standby_W.n: Drawn whenever the pack is live.

steering_pump_duty.n: Higher than trim: a slalom demands frequent correction.

steer_angle_min_deg.n: Monaco ENERGY_REQ_154 requires at least 40 deg each side. Exactly at the limit.

boat._note: Hull, propeller and course. Organiser-supplied catamaran hulls.

hull_length_m.n: COCKPIT DECK length, not the hull. Measured from Cockpit V1.3.stl. Used by tools/optimise_layout.py to bound the pack footprint. The hull is 5 m overall - see loa_m.

hull_width_m.n: COCKPIT DECK width, measured from Cockpit V1.3.stl.

hull_height_m.n: COCKPIT DECK height, measured from Cockpit V1.3.stl. Compare boat.freeboard_m of 0.45 m for the hull itself.

_waterline_note: hull_length_m / hull_width_m above are the COCKPIT DECK envelope used
by tools/optimise_layout.py to bound the pack footprint. They are not
the hull waterline. Annex I of the rules gives the boat as 5 m overall
length and 2.5 m overall width; the demihull waterline dimensions below
are what the resistance model actually needs, and until now they were
hard-coded defaults inside python/volare/boat.py rather than
parameters. Frictional resistance scales directly with Lwl and wetted
surface, so leaving the single most influential geometric input outside
the parameter file defeated the point of having one.

Lwl_m.n: Demihull waterline length. Annex I gives 5.0 m overall; the waterline is marginally shorter. Measure off the Annex II drawings to replace this.

Bwl_m.n: Demihull waterline beam. Overall boat width is 2.5 m across both hulls plus the gap.

beam_pitch_m.n: Annex I longitudinal distance between the two crossbeams. ENERGY_REQ_38 requires the cockpit clamps to straddle these.

buoyancy_L.n: ENERGY_REQ_2 requires 200 litres of buoyancy in the hulls.

cockpit_frontal_area_m2.n: Rasterised silhouette of 04_data/geometry/Cockpit V1.3.stl along the direction of travel. Was assumed at 0.42 m2, which was 52% high. Measured by projecting the mesh and counting the shadow, not by summing |n.a| over triangles - that double-counts every surface hidden behind another and overstates a closed body by roughly 2x.

cockpit_Cd.n: Streamlined pod. A blunt box is nearer 0.9.

cockpit_side_area_m2.n: Silhouette from abeam, from the STL. Sets the cross-wind heeling force, which nothing models yet.

cockpit_plan_area_m2.n: Silhouette from above, from the STL. This is the area available for the ENERGY_REQ_185 monitoring bay and any solar.

cockpit_surface_area_m2.n: Total wetted-by-air surface, from the STL. Sets the convective area for anything mounted against the shell, and the laminate area for the mass estimate.

cockpit_volume_L.n: Enclosed volume of the cockpit shell, from the STL. The pack envelope is 42.5 L of it.

cockpit_stl.n: 22082 triangles. The source of every MEASURED cockpit dimension in this section. Re-measure with python/volare/boat.py Cockpit.from_stl if the CAD changes.

beam_Cd.n: Circular cylinder in cross-flow. NOT 2.05, which is the square-section figure.

beams_faired.n: ENERGY_REQ_3 forbids modifying the organiser beams. A non-structural clip-on fairing is a separate question for the Technical Committee.

planing_transition_Fn.n: Volumetric Froude number at which the hull unsticks.

planing_LD.n: Lift/drag of the planing surface once up.

reverse_thrust_frac.n: Astern thrust as a fraction of ahead thrust at equal shaft power, for a propeller not designed for reverse. Drives the ENERGY_REQ_32 manoeuvrability check.

wind_speed_ms.n: Head-wind in the nominal performance case. Monaco sees an afternoon sea breeze; rerun the sweep at 5 m/s for the sensitivity.

displacement_kg.n: FLOATING mass - what buoyancy, planing lift and inertia respond to. ENERGY_REQ_48 caps everything EXCLUDING hulls at 250 kg; the hulls and beams are a further 65 kg (Annex I) and float too. The previous value of 250 kg silently omitted the hulls. Planing drag is directly proportional to weight, so that understated drag and overstated top speed. Built up in the mass section.

driveline_eff.n: Shaft, bearings and seals between the GEARBOX OUTPUT and the propeller. It was 0.97, which is a whole gearbox's worth of loss -- and the gearbox is already modelled explicitly in P50B_DrivetrainModel, whose reported shaft power is the gearbox OUTPUT. Applying 0.97 again on top of motor.gearbox_efficiency = 0.97 counted the same loss twice and cost about 3% of shaft power that nothing was actually consuming. Python's boat.py still applies the old value because it takes the 25 kW electrical cap as shaft power directly and never models a gearbox stage; the two are consistent about the boat even though they are not consistent about this number, which is exactly the sort of thing tools/crosscheck.py exists to keep visible.

pilot_mass_kg.n: Stated design value, 2026-09-11. The boat is weighed with the pilot (ENERGY_REQ_48), so this lands directly against the 250 kg cap. ENERGY_REQ_135 sets a 60 kg minimum ready to sail. Change this one value to re-plan the budget; cad/scripts/volare.py PILOT_DESIGN_KG must match and powertrain.py checks that it does.

air_density_kg_m3.n: ISA sea level, 15 deg C. Used for the aerodynamic pressure the cockpit and fairings are sized against. Monaco in July is warmer, so this is mildly conservative: density falls about 0.35% per kelvin, so 30 deg C gives about 1.16 and 5% less load.

air_kinematic_viscosity_m2_s.n: Round value used in note 01's Reynolds numbers. The ISA figure at 15 deg C is 1.47e-5, so this is 2% high and the Reynolds numbers 2% low. Kept because note 01's published Re values were derived with it and volare.py self-checks against them.

slam_load_g.n: Vertical slam acceleration the cockpit structure is sized to. No measurement supplied. Small planing craft see 3 to 6 g in a seaway; 3 g is at the lenient end and should be revisited once instrumented run data exists.

_note: Weight budget for ENERGY_REQ_48 and ENERGY_REQ_135.
The rule caps everything EXCLUDING the hulls at 250 kg, and the note
says the boat is weighed WITH the hulls and the pilot, hulls being
65 +/- 1 kg. So the check is:  weighed_total - 65 <= 250, and the
pilot counts against the 250.
Lines the model already computes (pack, outboard, trim) are NOT
repeated here - 08_compliance/P50B_MassBudget.m takes those from the
model so they cannot drift. Only items nothing else knows about live
here.
Every line is an ASSUMPTION until the part is on a scale. This budget
closes with very little to spare, which makes it the second tightest
constraint in the project after stored energy. Weigh things early.

cockpit_structure_kg.n: Deck, pod shell, bulkhead, longerons, motor mount. Composite build.

seat_kg.n: Seat with the headrest ENERGY_REQ_42 requires.

steering_control_kg.n: Wheel or bar, cables or hydraulics, throttle, trim switch.

hv_harness_kg.n: CABLE ONLY: 2.4 m of 150 mm2 plus the three-phase run, terminals and conduit. It used to be asked to cover the switchgear too, which is why the two lines below now exist.

energy_container_kg.n: The container AROUND the pack: shell, lid, seals, the ENERGY_REQ_155 overpressure valve, the 56 fire port and the 189 charge interface. It was missing from the budget entirely -- cad/scripts/powertrain.py builds it as a real box and the mass reconciliation caught the gap.

hv_switchgear_kg.n: Terminal box (1.4) and PDU with its contactors, fuse and shunt (4.2), from the CAD decomposition. Previously folded into the 4.0 kg harness allowance, which could not have covered it.

inverter_kg.n: Not selected - Competr lists the inverter on request. Representative device.

lv_system_kg.n: DC-DC, 12 V service battery, LV loom, breakers.

cooling_system_kg.n: Pump, seawater heat exchanger, hoses and about 2 L of coolant.

safety_equipment_kg.n: ENERGY_REQ_96 to 111: extinguisher and bracket, paddle, boat hook, flag, 10 m towline, bridle, horn.

organiser_equipment_kg.n: ENERGY_REQ_185 monitoring device, the organiser camera and their cabling. It is carried on race day whether or not the team fitted it.

fasteners_clamps_kg.n: ENERGY_REQ_38 beam clamps with gaskets, plus general fastening.

ballast_kg.n: ENERGY_REQ_135 ballast, only if the lightest pilot is under 60 kg ready to sail. Computed by P50B_MassBudget, not set by hand.

contingency_kg.n: Reserve against every line above being an estimate. Spend it deliberately, not by accident.

_note: Physical dimensions the Monaco rules put a number on.
Most of the technical rules are checked at scrutineering by a person
with a tape measure, not by a model. That does not make them
unmodellable - it makes them numbers the team has to commit to before
the tape measure comes out. Putting the intended value here turns a
checklist item into a check: the compliance module compares intent
against the rule and says which ones have no margin.
A value here means: this is what we intend to build. It is a
DESIGN_CHOICE until it is measured on the boat, at which point it
becomes MEASURED and the check becomes evidence.

bulkhead_fire_class.n: ENERGY_REQ_51, Euroclass. Changed from the French classification for 2026.

bulkhead_hole_diameter_mm.n: WITHDRAWN 2027: ENERGY_REQ_174/175 no longer exist. Retained as a design choice; 40 mm still satisfies the withdrawn 30-50 mm band. See docs/reference/RULES_CHANGES_2026_to_2027.md.

bulkhead_hole_capped.n: WITHDRAWN 2027: ENERGY_REQ_175 no longer exists. Retained as a design choice.

bulkhead_hole_offset_deg.n: WITHDRAWN 2027: ENERGY_REQ_176 no longer exists. Retained as sound practice; the hole still points to the pilot's side.

energy_container_to_pilot_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_25 requires at least 500 mm. Relaxed from 1 m for 2026.

overpressure_valve_aft.n: ENERGY_REQ_155, certified and adequately sized, facing aft.

external_charge_interface.n: ENERGY_REQ_189 - recharge without opening the container. New for 2026.

sensor_pass_through_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_182 requires at least 3.2 mm reaching cells at the core. Routed through one of the three free slots in the 4x4 grid.

estop_yellow_circle_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_76: red button over a 90 mm yellow circle.

estop_symbol_height_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_78 red spark on a white-edged blue triangle, at least 100 mm.

estop_from_starboard_m.n: ENERGY_REQ_85 requires within 1 m of starboard; 81 starboard and in front of the pilot; 86 facing outboard.

estop_isolates_telemetry.n: ENERGY_REQ_79 - all power sources, telemetry included, by relay and not in software.

contactor_dropout_ms.n: Main contactor mechanical opening time. From the contactor datasheet once one is chosen.

killcord_detect_ms.n: Switch debounce and detection. ENERGY_REQ_71 gives the whole chain under 1 s.

clamps_per_beam.n: ENERGY_REQ_38 requires at least two per beam, enveloping the full circumference.

clamp_width_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_38 requires at least 50 mm per clamp.

clamp_spacing_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_38 requires at least 750 mm, symmetric about the centreline. Tightened for 2026.

clamp_gasket_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_38 requires at least 1 mm of rubber between beam and clamp.

monitor_bay_open_to_sky.n: ENERGY_REQ_185: open to sky, outside every closed compartment, need not be waterproof.

_note: Hull resistance and contra-rotating propulsor, from the hydrodynamics
team's MEBC coaxial CRP design tool. The delivery is held in
04_data/hydrodynamics/ -- README, design report, blade geometry.
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS AND WHY IT MATTERS
Until this merge the resistance model was parametric: a Holtrop wetted
surface, an ITTC friction line, a wave-making hump and a Savitsky
planing term, all inherited from python/volare/boat.py. The
hydrodynamics team supplied a MEASURED resistance curve, and the two
disagree badly:
speed      supplied      parametric
The parametric model was applying a PLANING model to a slender
catamaran demihull that does not plane. At 5 m by 0.45 m the demihull
is L/B of about 11 -- a semi-displacement slender hull whose
resistance rises smoothly, with no wave-making hump to speak of and no
planing plateau at all. The Savitsky term alone was contributing a
constant 585 N above 20 km/h that is simply not there.
The supplied curve is therefore the default, and the parametric model
is kept only as a fallback beyond the data and as a comparison. This
is the single largest correction in the project's hydrodynamics.
WHAT THE CURVE DOES NOT COVER
It stops at 20 knots and it is for 250 kg. Our floating mass is 315 kg
(see boat.displacement_kg), and the hydrodynamics team's own report
says the 300 kg case has no supplied data and cannot be considered
validated. Both codebases independently took the ENERGY_REQ_48 limit
of 250 kg as the boat's displacement; it is the mass EXCLUDING the
65 kg of hulls and beams, which float too. The correction is a
26 percent increase in displacement, and resistance is not weakly
dependent on it.
So: trust the curve to 20 knots at 250 kg. Beyond that, and at our
real displacement, P50B_HullModel says out loud that it is
extrapolating.

resistance_source.v: MEBC Energy Class supplied resistance curve
resistance_source.n: Bare hull, 250 kg, LCG 1.80 m. Reproduced by the hydrodynamics team's tool as a hard assertion in its main.m stage 1.

resistance_displacement_kg.n: The condition the curve was measured at. NOT our floating mass.

resistance_LCG_m.n: Longitudinal centre of gravity for the supplied condition.

resistance_speed_kn.n: The five supplied points. There are no more.

resistance_bare_hull_N.n: Bare hull. Drive-leg and appendage drag are added separately.

resistance_max_valid_kn.n: The curve is not extrapolated silently. Above this the hull model reports that it is estimating.

drive_leg_drag_N_at_20kn.n: Submerged drive leg, from the hydrodynamics team's appendage model (0.15 m strut chord, flat-plate friction plus form factor). Their report flags it as NOT validated and notes it is unknown whether the supplied 624 N already includes it -- they add it, so we add it.

_propulsor_note: The Competr outboard datasheet says counter-rotating, so the single
Wageningen-style propeller in P50B_Propeller was always a stand-in.
The hydrodynamics team solved the real thing: blade element momentum
per rotor with Prandtl tip and hub losses, coupled through slipstream
contraction and swirl transport, with the shaft speed solved to meet
the required thrust exactly rather than left as a free variable.
The numbers below are their optimised submerged 3/3 design. It is a
preliminary design from BEM with empirical corrections, not CFD, and
their report is explicit that the section polars are the largest
single source of uncertainty in the absolute efficiency.

propulsor_type.n: Their trade study puts submerged ahead of surface-piercing by 58% at 20 kn, but says the verdict is dominated by the ventilated-section and drive-leg assumptions and is not settled without CFD.

propulsor_design_speed_kn.n: The point the propulsor was optimised at. 37.0 km/h.

crp_efficiency.n: CRP SYSTEM efficiency at the design point, not the isolated-rotor figure. The isolated rotors are 0.7942 each; quoting that as the system number would overstate it.

crp_thrust_N.n: Total, both rotors, at 20 kn. Required was 784.0 N.

crp_shaft_power_W.n: Total shaft power at the design point.

crp_energy_Wh_per_nm.n: 302.2 Wh/km. The objective the whole tool minimises.

front_diameter_m.n: 14.97 in. Well below the 21 in limit - the propulsor is profile-drag dominated, so it wants low blade area and low speed.

front_pitch_ratio.n: P/D at 0.7R. THEIR REPORT FLAGS THIS AS SITTING ON ITS SEARCH BOUND - the bound is setting the answer, not the physics. Widen and rerun before ordering.

rear_gear_ratio.n: Motor rev per rear-rotor rev. Different from the front - the gearbox has to deliver two ratios on a coaxial shaft.

axial_gap_m.n: Front-to-rear disk spacing. Sets the interference development factors g_dn = 1.254 and g_up = 0.733.

swirl_recovery_frac.n: Fraction of the front rotor's swirl recovered by the rear. This is what a contra-rotating pair is for, and the baseline equal-diameter equal-speed configuration got it badly wrong (-954%).

net_roll_torque_Nm.n: Front minus rear. A contra-rotating pair does not cancel roll reaction unless the torques match, and here they do not.

gearbox_input_rpm.n: Motor speed at the design point.

gearbox_efficiency.n: The hydrodynamics team's assumption. Ours in motor.gearbox_efficiency is 0.97; the difference is 1% on the whole chain and neither is measured. Their sensitivity ranks gearbox efficiency third out of ten inputs.

wake_fraction.n: Theirs. Ours in boat.wake_fraction is 0.06. Their sensitivity ranks wake fraction FIRST, at 14.7% spread on Wh/nm - it is the highest-value hydrodynamic measurement available.

thrust_deduction.n: Theirs. Ours in boat.thrust_deduction is 0.08. Ranked second at 14.4% spread.

controller_efficiency.n: Their lumped inverter figure. Our P50B_InverterData models the losses rather than assuming an efficiency, which is why the two chains do not agree exactly.

overall_efficiency.n: Effective hull power over electrical power, their whole chain at the design point.

cavitation_sigma_front.n: At 0.7R. No cavitation predicted by the analytical screen; margin 1.67.

blade_stress_front_MPa.n: Centrifugal plus bending, against an 83.3 MPa allowable. Safety factor 25. Preliminary analytical screening; FEA required.

_note: Physical envelopes and mounting positions for every powertrain
component, so the CAD is built from the same file as the analysis.
WHY THESE ARE HERE AND NOT IN THE CAD SCRIPTS
The geometry package under cad/ is a separate codebase with its own
canonical frame. If it carried its own component dimensions, the
project would have a fourth implementation of the design and the
same failure mode as the first three: a pack that is 709 mm long in
MATLAB and 700 mm long in Blender, agreeing until somebody edits one.
So the CAD reads this. cad/scripts/powertrain.py asserts that every
envelope it draws matches the value here, and fails if not.
POSITIONS ARE IN THE CANONICAL BOAT FRAME
X forward, Y port, Z up, origin = centreline x hull mid-length x hull
keel bottom. That is cad/scripts/volare.py's frame, NOT either
supplied STL's. The pod floor sits at Z = 577.7 mm and the pod runs
from X = -886.4 (tail) to X = +1651.3 (nose).
Positions are the CENTRE of each component's envelope unless the note
says otherwise. They are DESIGN_CHOICE: a layout the team intends,
not a measured build.
WHAT IS NOT MODELLED
Internal construction. A contactor is a box of the right size in the
right place with the right mass; it is not a magnetic circuit. The
purpose is envelope, clearance, routing, mass and centre of gravity --
the things that decide whether the boat is legal and whether the parts
fit. Anything needing internals belongs in the supplier's model.
_pack_note: The pack envelope is CALCULATED by P50B_Geometry from the cell
dimensions, clearances and enclosure wall thicknesses. It is not
repeated here -- the CAD calls the geometry model for it, so a change
to cell_clearance_m moves the box in Blender too.

pack_centre_mm.n: Sitting on the pod floor with the container lid 17 mm under the crown at its aft end. Moved forward and up from [-280,0,700]: the real pod floor aft is at 624 mm, not the 577.7 mm bounding-box figure, and the container was 30 mm into it.

pack_container_wall_mm.n: Container shell around the pack enclosure. Carries the ENERGY_REQ_155 overpressure valve, the 56 fire port and the 189 charge interface.

pack_container_pad_mm.n: Clear space inside the container beyond the pack: length for the terminal studs and the charge interface, width for the harness, height for the lid and the sensor route. Every one of the three was trimmed to make the container fit the pod -- it is the tightest thing in the boat after the mass budget.

inverter_size_mm.n: Representative liquid-cooled SiC drive for 400 A. NOT SELECTED -- Competr lists the inverter on request, so this is an envelope reservation, not a part.

inverter_centre_mm.n: Aft of the container, port, mirroring the PDU. Short three-phase run to the outboard, which is the point.

pdu_size_mm.n: Power distribution unit: main contactor, precharge resistor and contactor, HV interlock. One sealed box rather than parts scattered along the run, so ENERGY_REQ_60 and 63 are satisfied by one lid. 115 mm tall, not 130: the tallest thing inside is a 92 mm contactor, and the pod aft of the container gives 128 mm.

pdu_centre_mm.n: AFT of the container, low, starboard. It cannot go above the container: at that station the crown is 871 mm and the lid is at 854, leaving 17 mm. The aft compartment is 304 mm long and 160 mm tall at the transom, which is what actually sizes this box.

terminal_box_size_mm.n: HV terminal box on the container lid: main fuse (62 mm), shunt, and the pack terminal studs. 100 mm tall, not 120: the pod crown leaves 141 mm above the container lid at its forward end and the taller box could not be placed there, which pushed it into the aft bay the PDU needs.

terminal_box_centre_mm.n: On the container lid, forward, where the crown is 1012 mm and there is room for a 120 mm box. Directly over the pack terminals, which P50B_GroupLayout puts on the TOP face.

fuse_size_mm.n: 400 A class-aR HV fuse, bolt-down. Inside the PDU. Envelope typical of a 500 V DC traction fuse in this rating.

contactor_size_mm.n: Main DC contactor, gas-filled, 500 A continuous. Inside the PDU. ENERGY_REQ_79 requires the E-stop to open it by relay, not in software.

precharge_contactor_size_mm.n: Precharge path. Without it, closing the main contactor onto the inverter's DC-link capacitance welds the contacts.

shunt_size_mm.n: Current shunt. Feeds both the BMS and the Annex III telemetry current channel.

dcdc_size_mm.n: 1 kW HV to 12 V, from the Competr datasheet's auxiliary rating. Also supplies the ENERGY_REQ_184 organiser interface.

dcdc_centre_mm.n: On the container lid, starboard of the terminal box.

lv_battery_size_mm.n: 12 V 7 Ah LiFePO4 service battery. ENERGY_REQ_7 note 3 exempts it from the energy calculation; ENERGY_REQ_58 still requires it fused and ENERGY_REQ_67 still requires its temperature monitored.

lv_battery_centre_mm.n: Forward of the bulkhead with the LV electronics, clear of the HV container.

vcu_size_mm.n: Competr control unit, IP67. Datasheet section 2: 260x160x90 mm, 1x 35-way and 1x 23-way sealed connectors.

vcu_centre_mm.n: Forward of the bulkhead, in the ENERGY_REQ_62 IP56 compartment.

motor_centre_mm.n: Transom-mounted, just aft of the pod tail at X = -886 mm. The powerhead spans Z 100 to 900 mm and the leg hangs below it.

motor_shaft_angle_deg.n: Trim angle in the modelled pose. The datasheet allows -5 to +30 deg.

coolant_pump_size_mm.n: 12 V circulation pump, 8 L/min against the loop pressure drop.

coolant_pump_centre_mm.n: Beside the container, port, low so it stays primed. Half-width at this station is 286 mm.

heat_exchanger_size_mm.n: Seawater plate exchanger. The sea is the ultimate heat sink for both the pack loop and the motor.

heat_exchanger_centre_mm.n: Beside the container, starboard, low and near the through-hull pickup. Half-width here is 295 mm, so this is 15 mm off the skin.

coolant_hose_od_mm.n: 13 mm bore hose. Distinct from cooling.tube_id_m, which is the 6 mm passage inside the cold plates.

hv_cable_od_mm.n: 150 mm2 flexible tinned copper with silicone insulation, orange per ENERGY_REQ_61. Conductor alone is about 14 mm; the jacket dominates the bend radius.

hv_cable_bend_radius_mm.n: Six times outside diameter, the usual minimum for flexible HV cable. Sets whether a route is buildable, which is the whole reason the cables are modelled as swept curves rather than straight lines.

three_phase_cable_od_mm.n: Per phase, inverter to motor. Screened.

bulkhead_x_mm.n: Station of the ENERGY_REQ_50 bulkhead, moved aft from 120 mm with the seat. The pod is 350 mm half-width and 484 mm tall here, so the bulkhead spans a full section rather than a tapered one.

bulkhead_thickness_mm.n: Aluminium sheet on a non-combustible core.

bulkhead_width_mm.n: The pod's usable internal width at X = 120 mm: the shell half-width is 336 mm and 15 mm each side is reserved for the skin and fixings, leaving 642 mm. It was drawn 1400 mm wide -- twice the pod -- and then 660, which was still 10 mm over.

bulkhead_height_mm.n: Pod floor 633 mm to crown 1026 mm at X = 120 mm, inside the 15 mm skin allowance, is 393 mm. 380 leaves a fitting margin. It was 420, which put the bulkhead 9 mm into the floor.

bulkhead_z_mm.n: Centred in the 633 to 1026 mm opening at that station.

pilot_seat_x_mm.n: Seat back station. Moved forward from 700 mm. ENERGY_REQ_25 measures 500 mm from here to the container, and with the seat at 700 the container had to end by X = 200, which forced it into the tapering aft section where the pod is only 187 mm tall against the container's 218. Moving the pilot forward is also the right direction for trim.

pilot_seat_z_mm.n: Seat pan, just above the pod floor at 577.7 mm.

estop_centre_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_81 starboard and forward of the pilot, 85 within a metre of starboard, 86 facing outboard. Y is limited by the pod, which is 285 mm half-width at this station -- not by the rule.

monitor_bay_centre_mm.n: ON the crown over the cockpit, where ENERGY_REQ_185's open-to-sky and outside-every-closed-compartment conditions are both met and it is 400 mm clear of the nearest HV run. It was at X = -60, where the terminal-box cable came within 72 mm of the 100 mm the rule requires.

rules._note: Monaco Energy Class Technical Rules 2026.1. Numeric limits only; the full check including procedural items is in 08_compliance/.

temp_warn_fraction.n: ENERGY_REQ_68: warn at 90% of the maximum monitored temperature.

monitor_volume_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_185 free volume for the organiser device, open to sky.

_limits_note: Every numeric limit the 2026 rules impose, so no threshold is ever a
bare literal in MATLAB, Python or the browser engine. The requirement
number is in the note of each one; 08_compliance/P50B_MonacoCompliance
checks the design against these and nothing else.

hull_mass_kg.n: ENERGY_REQ_2 and Annex I: hulls with beams. Deducted from the weigh-in figure.

hull_mass_tol_kg.n: ENERGY_REQ_48 note: the hulls are supposed to be 65 +/- 1 kg.

pilot_min_mass_kg.n: ENERGY_REQ_135, ready to sail with overalls, helmet, lifejacket, shoes and comms. Below this the boat is ballasted.

bulkhead_hole_min_mm.n: WITHDRAWN 2027: ENERGY_REQ_174 no longer exists. Kept so the historical check still has a limit to report against.

bulkhead_hole_max_mm.n: WITHDRAWN 2027: ENERGY_REQ_175 no longer exists. Kept so the historical check still has a limit to report against.

killcord_max_cutoff_s.n: ENERGY_REQ_71 - instantly, less than one second.

monitor_min_cable_clear_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_185 - at least 10 cm from every power cable.

ip2x_threshold_dc_V.n: ENERGY_REQ_63 - circuits above 15 V DC or 6 V AC.

touch_probe_diameter_mm.n: ENERGY_REQ_60 - 100 mm long, 6 mm diameter insulated probe.

comms_min_range_nmi.n: ENERGY_REQ_142. VHF is forbidden for 2026 - ENERGY_REQ_141.

label_energy_threshold_Wh.n: ENERGY_REQ_171 to 173 apply to any battery above 100 Wh.

dt_s.n: Stepper timestep. Stable to ~8.5 s for the explicit browser scheme.

sigma_capacity.n: Ungraded batch spread. Grading to +/-1% gives 0.004.

sigma_resistance.n: Ungraded. This, not thermal feedback, is what drives current hogging.

population_correlation.n: High capacity tends to pair with low resistance.
